figures.finding: Norfolk Island's own council funds no film: its three grant programs are a community support program, a tertiary education bursary and a community strategic plan grant; Commonwealth Acts are in force there (Australia's offsets count spend there, found 2026-11-04: see the incentive).

sources.said: The three grant programs on offer are the Community Support Program, the Tertiary Education Bursary Program, and the Community Strategic Plan Grant Program.

15 Laws in force in the Territory After the final transition time, the laws in force in the Territory from time to time are: (a) Acts to the extent that they are in force from time to time in, or in relation to, the Territory; … 18A Application of New South Wales laws (1) Subject to this section and section 18B, the provisions of the law of New South Wales (whether made before or after the final transition time), as in force in New South Wales from time to time, are in force in the Territory.

figures.finding: Australia's production offsets count spend on Norfolk Island: the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997 counts goods and services provided in Australia (s 376-145) and takes Australia, in a geographical sense, to include Norfolk Island (s 960-505); the producer offset is 40% of a feature's qualifying spend, from A$500,000 of it (compilation in force from 1 October 2026).
figures.applies: Norfolk Island, as part of Australia for the Act.

sources.said: (1)Australia, when used in a geographical sense, includes each of the following: (a)Norfolk Island;

A company’s qualifying Australian production expenditure on a *film is the company’s *production expenditure on the film to the extent to which it is incurred for, or is reasonably attributable to: (a)goods and services provided in Australia; … The amount of the producer offset is: (a)if the *film is a *feature film that was produced for commercial exhibition to the public in cinemas—40%; or (b)otherwise—30%; … 1 A *feature film $500,000
